sources.quote: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada's ICT sector profile counts tens of thousands of firms, most with fewer than ten employees
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
sources.title: Canadian ICT Sector Profile 2024
sources.evidence: There are over 48,390 companies in the Canadian Information and Communications Technologies (ICT) sector and the large majority (over 44,870) fall within the software and computer services industries. The ICT sector consists mainly of small companies, with approximately 41,000 firms employing fewer than 10 people.

sources.quote: Registration on CanadaBuys, the federal tender portal run by Public Services and Procurement Canada through the SAP Business Network, is free
sources.title: How to register your business - CanadaBuys - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Before you can start bidding on tender opportunities posted by Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), you will need to register your business, which PSPC does using SAP Business Network, a web-based tool that allows businesses to view and bid on opportunities. Businesses can register in CanadaBuys by registering for a free SAP Business Network Account.

sources.quote: PSPC maintains a software as a service supply arrangement meant to simplify how departments buy SaaS
sources.title: About: Software as a service supply arrangement - Canada.ca
sources.evidence: Public Services and Procurement Canada (PSPC), on behalf of the Government of Canada, has issued a request for supply arrangement to establish a new method of supply to satisfy various software as a service (SaaS) requirements. The objectives of the SaaS supply arrangement are to simplify the procurement process to acquire SaaS solutions, establish pre-negotiated terms and conditions for contracts resulting from the vehicle, and increase competition and access to the latest SaaS solutions on the market for the GC.

sources.quote: in June 2026 the threshold bringing a procurement into scope dropped from $25 million to $5 million
sources.title: Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurements | CanadaBuys
sources.evidence: The Policy on Prioritizing Canadian Suppliers and Canadian Content in Strategic Federal Procurement, issued pursuant to the Buy Canadian Procurement Policy Framework, takes effect on December 16, 2025. Effective December 16, 2025: all Strategic Procurement $25M and up published after that date; and Effective June 15, 2026: all Strategic Procurement $5M and up published after that date.

sources.quote: section 52.1 extends that to software, including application software, where a French version exists
sources.title: Section 52.1 Disposition versions - Légis Québec (Charter of the French language, C-11)
sources.evidence: All computer software, including game software and operating systems, whether installed or uninstalled, must be available in French unless no French version exists. Software can also be available in languages other than French, provided that the French version can be obtained on terms, except price where it reflects higher production or distribution costs, that are no less favourable and that it has technical characteristics that are at least equivalent.

sources.quote: Administrative monetary penalties reach $10 million or 2 percent of worldwide turnover
sources.publisher: Commission d'accès à l'information du Québec
sources.title: Sanctions | Commission d’accès à l’information du Québec
sources.evidence: The Commission d'accès à l'information can impose administrative monetary sanctions on enterprises that violate certain obligations under the law on privacy. For entities other than individuals, the maximum penalty is $10,000,000 or the amount corresponding to 2% of the global revenue from the previous financial year if that amount is higher.

sources.quote: with mandatory breach reporting where there is a real risk of significant harm
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.title: What you need to know about mandatory reporting of breaches of security safeguards - Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.evidence: Organizations subject to PIPEDA are required to report to the Privacy Commissioner of Canada breaches of security safeguards involving personal information that pose a real risk of significant harm to individuals and notify affected individuals about those breaches. Real risk of significant harm is determined based on the sensitivity of the personal information involved in the breach and the probability that the personal information has been, is being or will be misused.

sources.quote: Supply Ontario runs enterprise wide vendor of record arrangements the same way
sources.title: Doing business with the Government of Ontario | ontario.ca
sources.evidence: The Government of Ontario's enterprise-wide Vendor of Record (VOR) Program provides goods and services commonly acquired by government ministries, with many available to other Provincially Funded Organizations, such as hospitals and municipalities. Agreements are established through open bidding, qualifying one or more vendors to provide goods or services for a defined period, on specified terms and conditions (including pricing); vendors interested in selling to government visit Supply Ontario for information about becoming a registered vendor.

sources.quote: Maximum penalties run to $1 million per violation for individuals and $10 million for organizations
sources.title: Frequently Asked Questions about Canada's Anti-Spam Legislation | CRTC
sources.evidence: The maximum amount of an administrative monetary penalty (AMP), per violation, for an individual is $1 million, and for a business it is $10 million.
